root_cause: ADR-T0658 §9 named this gap explicitly and deferred it: setUserEnabled(false) (T-0583) only blocks Keycloak from issuing a NEW access token to a deactivated employee — an access token issued BEFORE deactivation stays cryptographically valid until its own exp (Keycloak default TTL, ~300s). In that window the holder still passes AUTHENTICATION (withAuth — signature/exp check succeeds), even though every AUTHORIZATION path (T-0658/T-0662's ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL gate across all 7 authority resolvers) already denies them a grant. This task SHRINKS the authentication-side window by killing the KC SSO session + refresh tokens (no further access token can be minted from the live session) — it does NOT invalidate an already-issued access-JWT, which choros validates offline against JWKS (src/http/auth.ts) and which therefore stays accepted until its own exp; the guarantee in that residual window remains the PDP ACTOR_ACTIVE gate.
fix_summary: Added KeycloakUserPort.revokeUserSessions(userId) — POST /admin/realms/<realm>/users/<userId>/logout, live-confirmed against the t-0633-keycloak-1 dev container (204 on an existing user, 404 on an unknown one) using the SAME choros-registrar service-account token setUserEnabled already authorizes with (no new KC role/client). Called from PATCH /api/users/:employee_id's active:false branch immediately after setUserEnabled(false) succeeds. Deliberately BEST-EFFORT (never throws): a transient KC hiccup on this specific call must not fail the whole deactivation, because the PDP-side denial (T-0658/T-0662) is already unconditional and independent of this call's outcome — this is a defense-in-depth window-shrink, not a new security gate. The boolean outcome is written into the SAME user_account.deactivate audit event as payload.kc_sessions_revoked, so a failure is observable (not silently swallowed) without blocking the HR action. Reactivation is untouched — a fresh login creates its own new session, so there is nothing to revoke there (ADR §2.3).
test_methodology_note: Two layers: (1) src/__tests__/admin-port.test.ts AP-7 — a local stub HTTP server (no live KC) exercises the live adapter's request shape (POST to the exact /admin/realms/<realm>/users/<id>/logout path, Bearer token from the registrar client_credentials flow) and its never-throw contract across 204/200/404/500/connection-refused. (2) ci/checks/db/user-mgmt.db.test.ts — full HTTP-server + live Postgres :55432 (isolated cloned template DB per T-0147 convention) drives the ACTUAL PATCH route with InMemoryKeycloakUserPort standing in for KC (same pattern as the existing FF-583-4 test in this file), proving the call count, the audit payload, and — critically — that a revoke failure (failOnRevokeSessions) does not prevent deactivated_at from being set or the 200 response from returning. Separately, BEFORE writing any code, the live KC admin REST endpoint itself was sanity-checked with raw curl against the running t-0633-keycloak-1 container (choros-registrar client_credentials token → GET .../sessions → 200, POST .../logout on a real fixture user → 204, POST .../logout on a bogus UUID → 404) to confirm the exact status-code contract the port now codes against — this is documented in the ADR §2 rather than re-run as an automated test (no live-KC-required test was added to the suite; the stub-based AP-7 tests are what CI actually runs).
live_proof_plan: Dev stand was offline at task time (T-0702 build session), so the full UI→KC e2e was not run live end-to-end through the browser. HONEST EXPECTATION (R-1): /logout kills the KC SSO session + refresh tokens — it does NOT invalidate an already-issued access-JWT, which choros validates offline against JWKS (src/http/auth.ts) and which therefore stays accepted until its own exp (~300s realm TTL); the guarantee in that residual window is the PDP ACTOR_ACTIVE gate, not authentication. Plan for whoever runs it next: (1) log in to the product as a tenant owner, (2) in a SECOND browser session/incognito window, log in as a regular employee of that tenant and note their session is live (any authenticated page loads), (3) in the owner session, go to accounts management and deactivate that employee (PATCH /api/users/:id {active:false}), (4) cross-check via Keycloak admin console (Users → the deactivated user → Sessions) that the session list is empty IMMEDIATELY after step 3, not after a TTL wait — this is the direct observable effect of revokeUserSessions, (5) in the employee's still-open second session, confirm silent re-auth/token-refresh now FAILS (SSO session gone + account disabled — no new access token can be minted), and that within the residual ~5-min window of a cached access-JWT any privileged action is DENIED by the PDP layer (403/empty grants) even though bare authentication may still pass until exp, (6) confirm the audit_event row for user_account.deactivate (via GET /api/audit or DB) carries payload.kc_sessions_revoked:true for this real KC round-trip (proves the live HTTP path, not just the mock-covered code path).
